"What she has meant to our team, what she has meant to the league and what she's meant to women's basketball. She remains the tipping point."

Amber Cox on Caitlin Clark.

direct_replies.text: where have you been?   Why on earth did you not speak up before now?   Why why why have you taken this gift and not protected her.   Shameful you didn’t speak up immediately.

Saying this after you completely ignored (and likely participated in) a weeks long smear campaign in the media against Caitlin in the middle of the season is definitely a choice. Y’all have failed to have her back so many times. Put up or shut up. Sick of the blah blah blah with no action.

You’re about 2 1/2 years late with this, Amber!  You’ve let the WNBA treat her like crap when you should have filed charges and lawsuits against all of the players that have been trying to seriously injure her and other members of the team.  Unprofessional FO and coaches!
Where has this energy been the last three years? You could’ve prevented a lot of the gaslighting and frustration that her fans have shown by just acknowledging this from the very beginning.

Bullshit.  Sat idly by and watched her take shots literally and figuratively from media, league, coaches and other players.  Did nothing, said nothing.  In these prepared comments - spoke of the money and interest she generates but nothing of her generational skill set or record breaking accomplishments.  Your team has handcuffed and tried to hold her back - time to either let her go or build around her.

Amber Cox waited until the season was dead. Saturday she thanked Caitlin Clark for the buildings, thanked the fans, and tucked Stephanie White into a soft “we’ll grow.” She did not defend Clark while the hitting was still happening. She did not touch the whistles. She did not say A’ja Wilson crossed a line with a fan her own security later cleared. The flowers showed up after the coffin was shut.
That silence is the job. Clark is why the buildings filled. Say it the first time she gets dragged to the floor. Cox didn’t. And not only Clark. The rest of the Fever took the body shots, the joke officiating, the comments about who they were. Mitchell said the days were hard as hell. Cox’s answer was nothing. She protected no one.
The throat shot should have ended the quiet. On camera. No demand on the refs. No ban. No lawyers. Mama bear was nowhere. A thank-you after a first-round exit is a eulogy.
Same mute button on Wilson. A Fever player walks into the stands and the suspension machine spins. Wilson got a technical. The fan got sent back. Cox scolded the media, not the player who left the floor. No apology. “No basis in reality,” and the same day Brianna Turner and her own leading scorer said otherwise.
She ducked the culture too. Anti-heterosexual, anti-white, anti-Christian, anti-conservative, anti-woman, anti-American. Teams that will not stand for the anthem do not get a publicly backed floor. Call the congressman. Cut the tax dollars. Condemn the hate from every camp with the bite of a lion. Wilson bowed out late for FIBA, then showed up physical enough to decide a series. Cox did not ask how.
The roster is hers. No rim protector. No big once Aliyah Boston was in foul trouble. White still tinkering in the last week. She called the Aces a buzzsaw and did not prepare for one. Riding for players is not defending them. Those Vegas bench swaps, the scorers coming off while the game was still there, fit. Mitchell talked DMs and free agency, not the whistle.
Saturday was a confession. She knows Clark is the tipping point. She still would not name the officials, the throat shot, the anthem, or a teammate she had shielded.
Resign. Take White and the staff. Twenty-eight wins, sixth place, first-round exit. Continuity is an extension, not a plan. Her Saturday language was written so she wouldn’t have to.

I hardly know what to say.  The @WNBA has worked to downplay Clark since the minute she arrived.  No one would know who the Hell Amber Cox is if it wasn't for Clark. They are the worst sports league ever, and really, it is a woman's league, but they don't know what a woman is
